title: Made anxious
hookLine: the human was created anxious: fretful in harm, withholding in good (70:19–21)
carry: panic when it's bad, clutching when it's good

cards: Three in the morning. The heart is racing about an email you haven't answered, a bill, a lump that's probably nothing. And then, the next week, good news.
A raise. And instead of relief, a new worry: don't tell anyone, hold onto it, what if it goes. Panic when it's bad, clutching when it's good.
The Qur'an describes that exact pair in three short verses, and it doesn't describe a few nervous people. It describes the human being.

teach.b: Surah al-Ma'arij, verses nineteen to twenty-one. In Pickthall's translation: "Lo! man was created anxious."

teach.h: FRETFUL IN HARM, GRUDGING IN GOOD.
teach.b: Then the Qur'an explains its own word: fretful when evil touches him, and when good touches him, grudging. The Arabic for anxious is halu', a rare word.

Commentators noticed that the Qur'an defines it right away, in the next two verses, and many said that's the best explanation there is. Halu' is two things at once. Jazu': falling apart when harm comes.
Manu': holding tight, withholding, when good comes. Same nervous system, two directions. Notice the verb: created, khuliqa.

The Qur'an isn't saying some people are anxious because they've failed. It's describing how the human being comes, a worried creature, built that way, and its subject is al-insan, the human, not some humans.
That's honest, and it's gentle. It doesn't shame the anxiety. But it doesn't stop there either.
Verse twenty-two begins with one small word: illa, except. Except some people. Who they are is tomorrow's story; for today, just the diagnosis.
The panic at three in the morning and the clutching after good news are one trait, set down in three lines. What a person does with it is the question the next verses take up.

how: Muslim teachers often cite 70:19–21 to describe anxiety and stinginess as part of human nature, and point to the verses that follow, about steady prayer and giving, as the Qur'an's answer to them.

o: nervous only around strangers and crowds
created halu': fretful in harm, grudging in good
anxious about money above everything else

p: anxious, the word the Qur'an defines

s: the verse says only weak people are anxious
it says the human being was created anxious.
the Qur'an defines halu' in the next two verses
fretful in harm, grudging in good.
the passage ends with the diagnosis
verse 22 turns with 'except', and names who is different.

games.q: good news arrives: a raise. by 70:21, what does the anxious human tend to do?
games.why: manu': grudging, holding tight. the same anxious nature that panics in harm clutches in good.

practice: Scan gently for anxiety: a tight jaw, a busy stomach, a thought that keeps circling.

Wherever you find it, don't argue with it or scold yourself; just name it quietly, anxious, made this way, and breathe out a little longer than you breathed in. You're not fixing it today, only seeing it clearly.

wordCard.voice: Made anxious. In 70:19–21 the human is created halu': fretful when harm comes, grudging when good comes. A description, not a verdict. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 70:19: anxious, impatient; a rare word the Qur'an explains in the next two verses.
